title: PDP-11 word width
text: The PDP-11/70 uses 16-bit words and 8-bit bytes.

title: PDP-11/70 virtual addresses
text: A PDP-11/70 program uses 16-bit virtual addresses: 64 KiB per address space. Separate instruction/data spaces do not make an individual virtual address wider.

title: PDP-11/70 physical addresses
text: The PDP-11/70 MMU produces 22-bit physical addresses. The 4 MiB address range includes reserved device space; it does not imply 4 MiB of installed RAM.

title: PDP-11/70 register roles
text: R7 is the program counter (PC); R6 is the stack pointer (SP). The /70 has separate Kernel, Supervisor and User stack pointers and two sets of R0–R5.

title: Autoincrement deferred
text: @(Rn)+ is autoincrement deferred, mode 3: fetch a word pointer and increment the register by two, including for a byte operand. It differs from (Rn)+, mode 2.

title: MOVB to a register
text: MOVB sign-extends a byte when the destination is a register. This is not the rule for every byte instruction or a byte stored in memory.

title: Autodecrement ordering
text: INCB -(R0) decrements R0 by one before using it as the byte address; INC -(R0) decrements R0 by two before accessing the word.

title: Interrupt vector contents
text: A PDP-11 interrupt vector contains two words: new PC, then new PS at vector address plus two. It is not just a handler address or a single instruction.

title: UNIX V7 listing order
text: In UNIX V7, ls -t sorts by modification time, newest first; -r reverses ordering. Thus ls -tr lists oldest first.

title: UNIX V7 output redirection
text: In V7 sh, > creates or truncates the output file; >> appends or creates it. These operations can change guest files.

title: VT52 and ANSI cursor positioning
text: VT52 direct cursor addressing uses ESC Y followed by row and column characters with octal 040 added. ANSI CUP uses ESC [ with numeric parameters and H. They are different protocols.

title: Guest terminal and simulator monitor
text: A dedicated guest serial line is distinct from the GNU Screen operator console and SIMH monitor. Neither a reused TCP port nor a terminal label proves guest identity.

title: Emulated device and guest driver
text: SIMH device availability does not establish that the guest has the matching driver. A quiet browser does not prove a stopped CPU.
